sources.publisher: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
sources.note: 2027 Application Guidelines for Research Students: eligibility, benefits, documents, screening, placement, notes (read in full, 11 pages)

summary: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Research Students is run by Japan's education ministry for international students who want to study in a graduate course at a Japanese university as research students. Candidates apply through the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country of nationality (the embassy recommendation route). The scholarship gives a monthly allowance, waives entrance exam, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides economy-class flights to and from Japan. The 2027 call is for arrival in April 2027 or September/October 2027.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality: you must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. People with Japanese nationality at the time of application are not eligible, except dual nationals who live outside Japan and choose the other nationality and give up Japanese nationality by the date of arrival in Japan; they must be screened at the Japanese mission of the country whose citizenship they choose.

Age: in principle you must have been born on or after 2 April 1992. Exceptions are limited to cases where MEXT judges that you could not apply in time because of conditions in your country (for example military service or loss of education due to war). Personal circumstances such as finances, family or health are not accepted as reasons for an exception.

Academic background: for a master's course or the first phase of a doctoral course you need 16 years of school education outside Japan, or a programme of at least three years at a university abroad with a degree equivalent to a bachelor's, or you must otherwise qualify for entry to a Japanese graduate school. For the second phase of a doctoral course you need an overseas master's or professional degree, or a university degree plus at least two years of research at a university or research centre with academic ability equal to a master's holder as recognised by the graduate school. For doctoral courses in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and certain pharmaceutical fields you need 18 years of school education abroad, or a programme of at least five years with a degree equivalent to a bachelor's, or 16 years of education plus at least two years of research and recognised equivalent ability. Check each university's website, because the required background varies by university. You are eligible if you will definitely meet the condition by the time of enrolment.

Field of study: apply in the field you majored in at university or a related field, and it must be a subject that can be studied in a Japanese graduate course. The Japanese mission in your country may restrict the fields. Traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki and classical Japanese dance, and subjects that need practical training in specific techniques at factories or companies, are not covered. Students of medicine, dentistry or welfare science cannot do clinical training such as medical care or operative surgery until they hold the relevant Japanese licence.

Language and health: you must be willing to learn Japanese and interested in Japan, and able to do research and adapt to life there. You must submit a health certificate in the prescribed form signed by a physician saying you have no physical or mental condition that would hinder study in Japan.

Arrival and visa: you must choose either the April term (arrival between 1 and 7 April 2027, departure not before 1 April 2027) or the October term (arrival within two weeks before or after the start of the university's term, September or October). The choice generally cannot be changed after submission. You must, in principle, obtain a new Student visa at the Japanese mission in your country of nationality before travelling, even if you already hold another Japanese residence status.

Not eligible: military personnel or military civilian employees at arrival or during payment; people who cannot arrive by the specified last date; previous MEXT grantees (with exceptions, for example more than three years of study or work between the earlier scholarship and this one, past Japanese Studies students who are graduating, and some other programmes); people also applying to another MEXT programme; people already enrolled in Japan on a Student visa, or planning to enrol privately before payment starts (with an exception for those who will verifiably finish before payment starts); people planning to receive other Japanese government or related scholarships; people expected to graduate who cannot meet the academic condition by the deadline; dual nationals who cannot show they will give up Japanese nationality; people who change residence status away from Student; people planning long-term fieldwork or internship outside Japan or long leave from the university; people with no intention of obtaining a degree in Japan; and people found cheating in the written exam.

Other expectations: grantees are expected to join school and community activities, stay in touch with their Japanese university after graduating, answer surveys, and help with events run by the Japanese mission after returning home.
age_experience_notes: Born on or after 2 April 1992 in principle (limited exceptions for conditions in the home country). No work experience is required; applicants who are employed submit a recommendation letter from their present employer. Doctoral second-phase and medicine-type doctoral routes need two years of research experience if you do not hold the relevant degree.
funding_summary: MEXT pays a monthly allowance of JPY 143,000 for preparatory-education and non-regular students, JPY 144,000 for regular master's or professional degree students, and JPY 145,000 for regular doctoral students, plus JPY 2,000 or 3,000 for those in specially designated regions. Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees are waived. MEXT provides an economy-class ticket to Japan and, on application, a ticket home. Non-regular students are funded from April or September/October 2027 to the end of March 2029; regular students are funded for the standard period of their course, with a 6-month Japanese preparatory period added when the university thinks it is needed. Amounts may change each fiscal year.
programmes_note: Research students are those in a master's, doctoral or professional graduate course at a graduate school (regular students), or doing research in a specialised field at an undergraduate department, graduate school or university institute with the aim of completing a course (non-regular students), or in preparatory Japanese-language education. You apply for your own major or a related field; individual field names are not listed. Excluded fields are listed under eligibility.
institutions_note: No universities are named. Applicants who pass the First Screening contact Japanese universities themselves to ask for a letter of provisional acceptance. The Placement Preference Application Form lists up to three universities, but you may obtain at most two letters of provisional acceptance and may contact at most two universities at the same time. MEXT consults the universities and places grantees; a national university is prioritised over a private or non-national public one, regardless of your preference order.

summary.detail: Master's or professional graduate course at a Japanese graduate school. Standard period of study is two years after a university degree (some courses more than one year but less than two); professional degree courses are two years (graduate law schools three years). Regular students receive JPY 144,000 per month; non-regular students and those in preparatory education receive JPY 143,000. Non-regular students are funded until the end of March 2029. Fields must be your major or a related field.
summary.source_text: Master's degree course; Professional degree course

summary.detail: Doctoral course at a Japanese graduate school: three years after a master's course; in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and pharmacy (6-year undergraduate base) most universities offer only 4-year doctoral courses, which need 18 years of school education. Regular doctoral students receive JPY 145,000 per month. Regular master's students who want to continue to a doctoral course must apply for an extension of the scholarship period and pass the graduate school entrance exam.

benefits.limit_text: JPY 143,000 per month (preparatory education and non-regular students); JPY 144,000 (regular master's or professional degree students); JPY 145,000 (regular doctoral students); plus JPY 2,000 or 3,000 per month in specially designated regions
benefits.conditions: Amounts may change each fiscal year. Payment is suspended for long absences from the university. The first payment comes one to one and a half months after arrival, so the guidelines recommend bringing about USD 2,000. Payments go to a Japan Post Bank account opened after arrival.

benefits.limit_text: Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees waived
benefits.conditions: The entrance examination fee is paid by the grantee if the grantee cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted.

benefits.limit_text: Economy-class flight to Japan from the international airport closest to your residence, and an economy-class flight home on application
benefits.conditions: Only if you arrive in the specified period and return by the end of the final month of the scholarship. Not covered: travel to your home airport, airport taxes and fees, travel within Japan, travel insurance, and carry-on or unaccompanied baggage. If you must travel via a third country to get a visa or there is no direct flight, MEXT pays the flights but you pay lodging and travel costs in the third country. No return ticket if you return early for personal reasons or stay on in Japan.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation costs are paid by the grantee
benefits.conditions: Some universities have residence halls for international students, subject to limited rooms; others live in regular dormitories or private housing. Housing is hard to find for grantees with dependants, so arrive alone first.

benefits.limit_text: Grantees must enrol in National Health Insurance on arrival; who pays the premiums is not stated
A 6-month Japanese-language preparatory period for those who need it, included in the funded period
benefits.conditions: Decided by the accepting university or MEXT based on the language exam.

requirements.text: Application Form for 2027, with a clear photograph 4.5 x 3.5 cm taken within six months (upper body, full face, no hat, name and nationality written on the back). Number the documents in the upper right corner of the first page. Original plus 2 copies unless a document says otherwise.
Placement Preference Application Form for 2027, submitted to the Japanese mission first with the application and again after you obtain provisional acceptance letters.
Field of Study and Research Plan on the 2027 form, describing past and present field of study and your research theme and plan in Japan; it is an important reference for placing you at a university.

Academic transcript for all academic years of the university attended, issued by the university or the national government, showing the grade scale and grades for every subject each year. Graduates of a graduate programme submit undergraduate and graduate transcripts. A degree certificate or class-rank certificate does not replace a transcript.

Certificate of graduation or degree certificate, or a certificate of prospective graduation if you have not yet graduated. Graduates of both levels submit both. An attested copy is acceptable; originals are not returned.
Recommendation letter from the president, dean or academic adviser at the current or last university attended. Free format; a sample exists.
Medical certificate on the 2027 form, completed and signed by a physician. Tell the Japanese mission promptly if your health changes after submission.
Abstracts of theses or papers (abstracts of the graduation thesis and presented papers are acceptable), with your name on the first page.
Certificate of Japanese or English proficiency, 3 copies (no original), issued no earlier than two years before the application date; record it in sections 21 and 22 of the application form.
Recommendation letter from your present employer, 3 copies, free format.
Photographs of your own works of art or a digital recording of a musical performance.
requirements.conditional_rule: if majoring in fine arts or music

requirements.text: Documents not in Japanese or English need a translation in one of those languages. Submitted documents are not returned. Submit to the Japanese embassy or consulate general of your nationality, not to MEXT.

application_steps.title: Read the guidelines and contact your Japanese mission
application_steps.detail: The call opens around mid-April at each Japanese embassy or consulate general; for the 2027 intake, submissions ran around early May to late July 2026. The deadline and the process differ by country, so confirm them with the mission in your country of nationality.

application_steps.title: Prepare and submit the application set
application_steps.detail: Complete the application form, placement preference form, field of study and research plan, medical certificate and recommendation letter and gather transcripts and certificates. Submit by the mission's deadline to the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country of nationality. Do not send documents to MEXT.

application_steps.title: First screening at the Japanese mission
application_steps.detail: The mission checks your documents, gives written language exams in Japanese and English (English may be exempted where English is an official language) and holds an interview. Documents must show academic results above a certain level and a detailed research plan. The interview checks your sense of purpose, knowledge of Japanese universities and ability to talk with an adviser in Japanese or English. Dates and results vary by mission; reasons are not disclosed, and passing does not guarantee selection.

application_steps.title: Request letters of provisional acceptance
application_steps.detail: If you pass, you contact Japanese universities yourself, starting with the international student office, after the results and not later than 1 September 2026 (Japan time) for the 2027 call. Send the passing certificate and the stamped copies of your documents by email. You may contact at most two universities at a time and obtain at most two letters; a letter greatly influences the final result, and universities generally need about one month to issue it.

application_steps.title: Submit the placement preference form
application_steps.detail: Around mid-September to early October 2026 (the deadline varies by mission) you submit the final Placement Preference Application Form, listing up to three universities based on the replies you received. Universities that declined you cannot be listed. If you have no letter you can still submit, but your arrival is limited to the October term.

application_steps.title: Second screening by MEXT and results
application_steps.detail: From November 2026 MEXT holds the second screening and places you at a university that agrees to accept you; if none accepts, the application is rejected. Results and your accepting university are notified through the Japanese mission from January to early March 2027, without reasons, and objections to the placement are not accepted.

application_steps.title: Get a Student visa and arrive in the set period
application_steps.detail: Obtain a new Student visa at the Japanese mission in your country before travelling and arrive in the specified period (1 to 7 April 2027 for the April term, or within two weeks of the university's term start for the October term). Arriving outside it means no travel expenses are paid; a grantee who cannot arrive in time must withdraw except in unavoidable cases. Learn Japanese before departure.

application_steps.title: Study, keep conditions and finish the course
application_steps.detail: Open a Japan Post Bank account, enrol in National Health Insurance and begin Japanese preparatory education if required. Payments can be suspended or cancelled, and part or all of the money may have to be repaid, for false statements, breaking the pledge, serious legal or disciplinary problems, poor results that make finishing on time impossible, changing residence status, unapproved other scholarships, or moving up a level without an approved extension. To proceed from master's to doctoral study you must apply for an extension and pass the entrance exam.

application_steps.title: Return home and stay in touch
application_steps.detail: On application MEXT provides an economy ticket home if you graduate and return by the end of the final scholarship month. After returning, grantees keep close relations with their university, cooperate with surveys, and help with events run by the Japanese mission.

not_stated: Teaching language of the graduate courses (set by each university; the guidelines mention Japanese and English only in the exams and the interview)
Exact deadlines and exam dates per country (set by each Japanese mission)
Minimum grade or GPA (only 'a certain level' of academic achievement is stated)
Who pays National Health Insurance premiums
A list of countries or of universities taking part
